category_title: Students with intellectual disabilities who exhibit disruptive behaviors (hitting, making sounds, damaging property)
student_description: This student is frequently unresponsive to verbal instructions and exhibits physical aggression or property destruction when seated near peers. They require a highly structured approach utilizing visual rewards, deliberate wait time, non-verbal behavioral corrections, and proactive peer education to foster a supportive environment.

criteria.rationale: The student is often unresponsive to verbal interaction but responds positively to visual markers of success.
criteria.check: The tutor provides or suggests a visual or tangible reward (such as drawing a star on the student's work) when the student follows directions.

criteria.rationale: Rapid verbal prompting fails for this student; they require a brief, silent pause to process instructions and refocus.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly incorporates a pause or wait time (e.g., waiting 4-5 seconds) after giving an instruction or when the student becomes distracted.

criteria.rationale: Reacting verbally to every negative behavior disrupts the class, whereas non-verbal cues effectively communicate boundaries to this student.
criteria.check: The tutor uses non-verbal communication (e.g., sad facial expressions, shaking head, or gentle physical touch) to address negative behavior before or instead of using verbal reprimands.

criteria.rationale: When the student exhibits aggression, they need immediate, one-on-one feedback explaining how their actions physically or emotionally affect peers.
criteria.check: The tutor addresses aggressive behavior by establishing one-on-one contact (e.g., mutual eye contact) and explicitly stating that the behavior hurts peers or makes them uncomfortable.
